newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen falling as confidence wanes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen falling as confidence wanes.

text.p: Thai stocks were seen moving down as confidence in Thailand's economic management and the travails of the baht continued to erode investor sentiment, analysts said.

The SET Index fell sharply lower on Monday as the Thai baht's continuing weakness led investors to sell and send the SET Index 16.64 points or 2.65 percent lower to close at 611.91 points. The SET 50 index fell 1.60 points to 45.52.
"I think we are in for a period of extreme volatility, but short of an IMF bailout I think the market should come down," said George Morgan, country manager of ABN Amro Hoare Govett.
"I think the chances of the situation of having to be resolved by an IMF bailout are getting greater," he said.
The market would probably react positively to IMF assistance to resolve Thailand's financial woes but its involvement was not guaranteed and could be some months away, Morgan said.
But a growing crisis of confidence among foreign bankers was making an IMF program or at least a credible domestically-managed economic package more pressing, he said.

Despite the worries some funds are so underweight in Thailand they are expected to continue picking up discounted blue chips on weakness, although most are sidelined waiting for the currency to stabilise, analysts said.
The recently-floated baht fell to a record low of 30.80 per dollar in the domestic market on Monday causing the central bank to intervene to halt the slide.
